control.text: Build web applications with ePage Studio
Design pages visually, write JavaScript for browser interactions and server-side logic, and publish your project with eServer. This website is built with ePage.
Arrange controls visually, adjust their properties, and use layouts and layers to organize each page.
Use JavaScript for control events. When an action needs eServer, a Task Set groups request preparation, server logic, and the browser response in one named operation.
Register your project directory in eServer. It reads your page definitions and serves the application over HTTP or HTTPS.
Turn a Div into a reusable component
Combine child controls with your own properties, methods, and events. A single multiline Edit component can then serve several views, with its own font, height limit, and behavior in each one.
See how Faith builds its Edit component
Connect a page to eServer with Task Set
When a visitor submits a form, a Task Set can read the input in the browser, validate and process it on eServer, then display the result in the page. All three scripts are stored with the page.
Try a Task Set and read the three scripts

Each page has its own directory. Its page.xml stores the visual controls and the page's client-side and server-side code. Images and other page assets can live beside that file. At the project root, project.xml lists the pages and resources.
